stem: A hypothetical pair of homologous chromosomes has markers arranged A-B-C and a-b-c at matching gene locations. A single reciprocal exchange produces A-b-c and a-B-C. Marker order is preserved, and no sequence change occurs outside the exchanged segments. Which of the following best locates the exchange?

options.label: A
options.text: Before the first of the three marker loci
options.explanation: Exchanging the entire marked segment would preserve the three markers together as a block. It would not create the observed separation of the first marker from the others.
options.misconception: Places the exchange before the entire marker block even though the first marker separates from the others.

options.label: B
options.text: After the third of the three marker loci
options.explanation: An exchange beyond the marked region would leave these three-marker combinations intact. It cannot explain the observed mixing of parental origin within the displayed segment.
options.misconception: Places the exchange outside the marker block despite the observed change within it.

options.label: C
options.text: Within another chromosome lacking these loci
options.explanation: The altered combinations occur at the displayed matched loci. Exchanging a different chromosome would not account for the reciprocal change within this specified marker series.
options.misconception: Attributes a change in these marker combinations to an exchange on a different chromosome.

options.label: D
options.text: Between the first and second marker loci
options.explanation: The first marker retains its original association, while the second and third come from the other chromosome. That transition places the exchange between the first two loci.
options.misconception: No misconception: The switch in parental origin after the first marker locates the exchange boundary.

options.label: E
options.text: Between the second and third marker loci
options.explanation: An exchange here would change the association of the third marker while preserving the first two together. The observed second marker has also switched origin.
options.misconception: Keeps the first two markers together despite the observed change in the second marker’s parental origin.

context: Learning objective: infer a recombination interval from the transition in parental marker origin. The segment beyond the first marker has changed origin, placing the crossover between the first and second loci.
